T1.implementation_approach: Design a user-friendly interface using wireframes and mockups. Implement using frontend frameworks.
T1.notes: Focus on intuitive navigation and responsive design.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs for problem repository operations like create, read, update, delete.

T3.implementation_approach: Design schema for storing problem data including metadata, tags, and difficulty levels.
T3.notes: Optimize for query performance and scalability.

T4.implementation_approach: Develop a feature to allow users to submit code via a frontend form and store submissions in the backend.
T4.notes: Include validation for code format and size.

T5.implementation_approach: Implement a system to execute submitted code in a sandbox environment and compare outputs with expected results.
T5.notes: Ensure security and prevent malicious code execution.

T6.implementation_approach: Track user progress by storing completed problems and achievements in the database.
T6.notes: Provide APIs for fetching progress data.

T7.implementation_approach: Design a UI to display user progress using charts and tables.
T7.notes: Ensure data visualization is clear and interactive.

T8.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to fetch and update leaderboard data based on user scores.

T9.implementation_approach: Design a UI to display leaderboard rankings with filters and sorting options.
T9.notes: Ensure responsive design and real-time updates.

T10.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to manage hints and tutorials for problems.

T11.implementation_approach: Design a UI to display hints and tutorials with search and filter functionality.
T11.notes: Ensure tutorials are easy to navigate.

T12.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests for problem repository functionality.
T12.notes: Focus on edge cases and API validation.

T13.implementation_approach: Test code submission and evaluation system for accuracy and security.
T13.notes: Include tests for sandbox execution and malicious code handling.

T14.implementation_approach: Test user progress tracking for correctness and data integrity.

T15.implementation_approach: Test leaderboard functionality for real-time updates and accuracy.
T15.notes: Include tests for sorting and filtering.

T16.implementation_approach: Test hints and tutorials backend and UI for usability and correctness.
T16.notes: Ensure tutorials load quickly and are searchable.

T17.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using cloud services and CI/CD pipelines.
T17.notes: Ensure scalability and monitor performance post-deployment.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.title} ({self.difficulty})>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), nullable=False, unique=True)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), nullable=False, unique=True)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<User {self.username}>"

from app.database import db

class Solution():
    def __init__(self, id=None, problem_id=None, user_id=None, code=None, is_correct=None, submission_time=None):
        self.id = id
        self.problem_id = problem_id
        self.user_id = user_id
        self.code = code
        self.is_correct = is_correct
        self.submission_time = submission_time

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "problem_id": self.problem_id,
            "user_id": self.user_id,
            "code": self.code,
            "is_correct": self.is_correct,
            "submission_time": self.submission_time
        }

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_bp
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_bp
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_bp

def register_blueprints(app):
    app.register_blueprint(problem_bp)
    app.register_blueprint(user_bp)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_bp)

from flask import Flask
from app.database import db
from app.routes import register_blueprints

def create_app():
    # Create the Flask app instance
    app = Flask(__name__)
    
    # Configure the app (if any configuration is needed)
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

    # Initialize the database with the app
    db.init_app(app)

    # Register blueprints for routing
    register_blueprints(app)

    return app

from app import create_app

app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Repository: A comprehensive collection of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive automated feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Progress Tracking: Tracks user progress, including solved problems, attempted problems, and performance metrics.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings of users based on their problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Tutorials: Provides hints and tutorials for selected problems to help users improve their skills.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
